ops.title: Concurrent test runs contend on scripts/test.sh's process cap, NOT on DAEMONKIT_HOME
ops.body:
Correction (2026-08-04). Agent sessions have been serializing fleet test runs on
the stated grounds that "two suites contend on the process-global
DAEMONKIT_HOME." **That mechanism does not exist.** The serialization is still
right; the reason is different, and the wrong reason invites wrong workarounds
(e.g. "I'll point DAEMONKIT_HOME elsewhere and run concurrently" — which fixes
nothing).

## DAEMONKIT_HOME does not collide across runs

`internal/testhome.Sandbox` sets it with `t.Setenv`
(`internal/testhome/testhome.go:15-20` in cc-pool; same shape elsewhere).
`t.Setenv` mutates only the *test binary's own* process env, and `go test` gives
every package its own binary process, each pointed at its own `t.TempDir()`.
Two concurrent runs cannot collide there. `t.Setenv` also forbids `t.Parallel()`,
so sandboxed tests are already serial within a binary.

Checked for the other plausible cross-process collision — a user-global resource
keyed by a fixed name — and found none in cc-pool: no test invokes `launchctl`,
touches `~/Library/LaunchAgents`, or registers a `gui/` domain label. The fixed
`com.yasyf.cc-pool*` strings in tests are contract-test string assertions and
in-memory `trust.PeerRole`/`trust.Requirement` values, not registrations.

## The real constraint: the per-UID process cap

`scripts/test.sh` samples the current per-UID process count at start and sets
`ulimit -Su` to `cur + 400` (TEST_NPROC_HEADROOM). Two concurrent runs each spawn
children the other's cap did not budget for, so one run's spawns hit `EAGAIN`
and fail spuriously. Note the cap is computed once, at start — a second run
started later samples a `cur` already inflated by the first, so concurrency
loosens the safety margin as well as causing flakes.

Consequence: **an unexplained `EAGAIN` or resource-exhaustion failure means
"suspect an overlapping run before you suspect the code."** This is worst for
lanes working on teardown/reap paths (fusekit's holder, cc-pool's
accountterminal), where a spurious spawn failure is indistinguishable from a
real teardown bug.

## What is NOT corrected

AGENTS.md § Testing is unaffected and still binding: never bare `go test`,
always `scripts/test.sh`. The fork-bomb hazard it describes (self-exec TestMains
re-entering the spawn) is real and is exactly what the cap defends against — see
the 2026-06-24 mount-holder fork-storm incident, `ccn doc show ef281ea`. This
note narrows one claim about *concurrency between runs*, nothing about the
harness requirement itself.
